youtube_title: Michigan City's 1933 prison break: ten men, smuggled pistols, and John Dillinger
youtube:
In September 1933, ten men broke out of the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City, Indiana, with guns that had been smuggled in. 🔦 John Dillinger, paroled from that prison in May, helped plan it and had pistols hidden in a shipment to the prison's shirt shop. By the day of the break, Sept. 26, he was locked up again himself, arrested in Dayton, Ohio, four days earlier. The ten forced their way out at gunpoint, shooting a prison clerk, took a visiting sheriff hostage and fled in commandeered cars. Two weeks later, three of them walked into the jail in Lima, Ohio, posing as Indiana officers, and freed Dillinger; Sheriff Jess Sarber was shot and died that night. The gang lasted less than a year: federal agents killed Dillinger in Chicago in July 1934, and Harry Pierpont was executed that October. The prison, near Michigan City's lakefront, dates to 1860 and still holds inmates today, so view it from the road.
